correctness.confirmed_valid_subclaim: For d>=2, all probability vectors including boundary points, C_tr(rho_p)=sum_k|p_k-1/d|. This follows analytically from exact finite cyclic twirl and Fourier diagonalization.

correctness.proof_limits: The finite rational matrix counterexample is exact and decisive; no numerical sampling is used to infer the general theorem.
correctness.rationale: The all-dimensional statement C_tr(F diag(p) F†)=sum |p_k-1/d| is proved correctly by a cyclic twirl and Fourier diagonalization for every d>=2 and boundary spectrum. However the same final claim asserts a qutrit formula 4r max_k |cos(theta+2pi*k/3)| without imposing r>=0, while positivity permits negative r. Explicit exact counterexample r=-1/12, theta=0 gives eigenvalues 1/6,5/12,5/12, real positive density, trace coherence 1/3, and claimed right side -1/3. Hence one final claim containing that assertion is false as stated.

originality.rationale: A January 2026 primary paper establishes precisely the two nontrivial symmetry premises (circulant rho is fixed by the uniform cyclic quantum channel; every incoherent diagonal delta is sent to I/d). Standard CPTP trace-norm contractivity and Fourier diagonalization then give the entire all-dimensional formula as an immediate corollary. Explicit formula not printed verbatim does not confer novelty. The qutrit formula also has a sign defect at permitted negative r. Other special classes and the Resultary qutrit Schatten work are not the decisive source.
residual_risks: The 2026 channel paper does not print the trace-coherence formula verbatim; conclusion is implication-based, resting on standard trace-distance contractivity and Fourier diagonalization.
There may be yet earlier symmetry/twirl characterizations; earlier priority would reinforce coverage and is not required to reject originality.
If a separate external convention r>=0 were intended, the displayed qutrit formula would be correct after adding that hypothesis, but such a convention is not in the audited package.

evidence: Eq. (3.2) defines Phi(X)=d^{-1}sum_k S^k X S^{-k}, exactly the assigned cyclic twirl.

Contractivity of trace distance under CPTP Phi immediately proves optimum I/d; DFT diagonalization gives sum_k|p_k-1/d|.

Nevertheless, the only valid principal equation follows immediately from Xie-Zhang 2026 Eq.3.2 and Corollaries 3.6/4.2 plus standard CPTP trace-norm contractivity and elementary Fourier diagonalization. The qutrit clause is a direct three-number zero-sum simplification with an omitted sign assumption. It determines no genuinely unknown natural invariant beyond the established universal channel projection, and offers no separately motivated new structural boundary or result; correct reproducible instances alone would not confer independent research value.
